aggregates.text: UPDATE. $598,998 passed 8 to 4. The rule got no vote.
aggregates.note: the recorded tally, printed exactly as the claim carries it.

aggregates.text: Three of the four no votes wrote the rule.
aggregates.note: C04 states four members voted against and names all four. The THREE is C14 crossed with C04, the three of them who also sponsored the ordinance.

aggregates.text: All scanned license plate data is automatically deleted after 14 days.
aggregates.note: stated as 14 days on APD's own page, not derived.

aggregates.text: Traffic camera footage is overwritten every 3 to 5 days.
aggregates.note: stated as 3 to 5 days on APD's own page, not derived.
the same 14 days as C25, spelled out in the headline.

aggregates.text: How long a scanned plate lives. Deleted after 14 days, per APD's own page.
Traffic footage overwritten every 3 to 5 days
Two fourteen day windows. The same length, not the same thing.
aggregates.note: The FIRST window is C25's 14 days. The SECOND is September 1st (C03) to September 15th (C13), which is also 14 days. The slide labels the coincidence as a coincidence in the same type block rather than implying a cause.

A LOWER BOUND stated in the claim, not derived. Drawn as a chevron rather than a point for exactly that reason, and the unit, municipal traffic cameras, is carried in the label because the slide's whole job is that different numbers have different units.
